Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cellDIVER 1.0.0.9000

New features

  • Pseudobulk differential expression with edgeR, for every supported object class. Raw counts are summed per sample and group by SCUBA::pseudobulk() (the full cells x features matrix is never materialised) and tested with edgeR’s quasi-likelihood model by scDE::run_dge(test_use = "edgeR"). Independent designs (each sample in one group) fit ~ 0 + group; paired designs (samples contributing cells to both groups, such as cluster versus cluster within donors) fit ~ sample + group. The DGE tab offers edgeR in both marker identification (every group versus the rest) and differential expression mode, with a sample / replicate column picker that defaults to the configured patient_colname, and a live, metadata-only preflight that shows, per contrast, whether edgeR will run or the cell-level Wilcoxon test will be used instead. Contrasts without enough replication fall back automatically to the cell-level test within the same run; every row carries a Method column, the summary names the design and the fallbacks, the table can be filtered by contrast and method, and a second download provides the pseudobulk sample table behind each contrast.

  • .h5ad and .h5mu files open as file-backed SCUBA objects (served by SCUBA’s Julia engine) when that engine is available, and through reticulate otherwise; options(cellDIVER.h5_engine = "julia" | "reticulate" | "auto") forces the choice. File-backed MuData objects get the DGE tab, which stays hidden for MuData objects loaded through reticulate.

  • Hexbin plots. Two new plot types, HexDensity and HexFeature, bin cells on the projection into hexagons colored by cell count or by the mean, median or sum of a feature’s values (via the hextant package, now in Imports). They use the app’s continuous palette, with the lightgrey-to-blue default.

  • Zero-centered diverging palettes for feature, dot and hexbin feature plots: a three-color scale with its midpoint at zero.

  • Scale limits for every plot with a continuous color scale (feature, hexbin feature, hexbin density and dot plots): a two-handle slider sets the values at which the end colors are placed, bounded by the values shown on the plot; values outside the limits are drawn in the end colors. Diverging palettes get a “symmetric about zero” option. The limits can also be expressed as quantiles (percentiles of the plotted values), and on feature and hexbin feature plots can be applied to the underlying per-cell values before binning or plotting instead of to the color scale (requires hextant 0.1.0 for hexbin plots).

  • Every continuous palette is also offered in a reversed form, listed next to the original.

  • Differential expression can be run on several assays at once. The DGE tab gains an “Assays to Analyze” selector; results are combined into one table with an assay column that can be filtered.

  • “Choose Projection” menus now have an info tooltip linking to the documentation.

Dependencies

  • Seurat 5.5.0 or newer is now required. Seurat 5.5.0 added ggplot2 4 compatibility to its plotting code, which is why earlier releases pinned ggplot2 (<= 3.5.2). The cellDIVER test suites (unit, module and browser) pass on Seurat 5.6.0 with ggplot2 4.0.3.

  • presto is now declared as a dependency with github::amc-heme/presto in Remotes. scDE calls presto for differential expression, and upstream presto still calls GetAssayData(slot =), which SeuratObject 5.4.0 rejects as defunct, so every DGE test fails on current Seurat. The fork uses layer = instead. Install from the fork (or let Remotes do it) until that change is merged upstream.

Breaking change

  • run_cellDIVER() and run_config() no longer attach their dependencies to the caller’s search path. They previously called library() on roughly 25 packages (shiny, Seurat, dplyr, ggplot2 and others) as a side effect of being called, which changed the global environment of whoever launched the app. Code that relied on that — for example calling DimPlot() at the console after closing the app — must now attach the package itself, or qualify the call as Seurat::DimPlot(). The apps themselves are unaffected.

Bug fixes

  • Multi-assay DGE on SingleCellExperiment objects tests the selected alternative experiment instead of running the main experiment under its name: the selected experiment is swapped into the main position before the object is handed to scDE. For AnnData objects the cell-level test runs on the X matrix only (scDE’s scanpy backend cannot select an obsm modality), so other selected assays are skipped with a notice.

  • Per-cell cutoffs given as quantiles are resolved once over the per-cell values of every panel, as documented, instead of separately per split group or feature.

  • With a diverging palette or per-cell cutoffs and no explicit color limits, split feature panels and shared-scale feature panels keep the pooled range of the values shown, so the same value has the same color in every panel; with separate scales, each panel keeps its own legend title.

  • The symmetric color limits slider can be narrowed: moving one handle mirrors that handle instead of restoring the wider range.

  • Hexbin feature plots drop their titles when titles are switched off, also when the module supplies default custom titles.

  • The subset filter dialog no longer saves a categorical filter with no values. The confirm button was disabled client-side while the selection was empty, but a late refresh of the value choices could empty it after the button was enabled, and the resulting filter matched no cells. The server now keeps the dialog open and asks for at least one value.

  • The multi-contrast edgeR call now passes lfc_format = "log2", assays without a raw counts layer are skipped (with a notice) instead of being sent to edgeR, and a single failing assay shows scDE’s own message instead of a wrapper around it.

  • Dot plots no longer trigger the aes_string() deprecation warning from ggplot2; the mappings use the .data pronoun.

  • The feature picker (and other server-side selectize inputs) stayed empty on Shiny 1.12 and later. The plots and DGE tab bodies were rendered lazily on the tab switch that also sends their updateSelectizeInput(server = TRUE) choices, and newer Shiny delivers that update before the body exists. The tab bodies are now rendered up front.

  • Tooltips did not work: shinyBS only registers its assets when attached with library(), which cellDIVER no longer does, so every bsTooltip() failed in the browser with “shinyBS is not defined”. The resource path is now registered at startup.

  • Plot download handlers logged “argument is of length zero” for every plot on startup, because their content type was computed from the file type input before it existed. The type is now inferred from the filename and the file type defaults to png.

  • Package code now declares its imports in NAMESPACE. 28 of the 40 packages in Imports had no import directive, so every cellDIVER function depended on run_cellDIVER() having attached its dependencies first. Calling anything outside a running app failed with could not find function; for example cellDIVER:::load_config(path) could not run at all.

  • adt_threshold_assay() and update_object_metadata() now work for SingleCellExperiment objects. They called assay(), colData<- and altExp<- unqualified, so both failed outside a running app.

  • Plot download buttons now produce a file. The download control sits inside a collapsed dropdown, and Shiny suspends outputs whose element is hidden, so the server never issued a download URL and the button stayed disabled.

  • make_subset() raised could not find function "error" instead of reporting an unrecognised numeric filter mode.

  • two_column_layout() raised object 'left_column' not found on every call, from a misspelled parameter, and emitted an invalid width: ,50,%; style.

  • Reading .h5ad and .h5mu objects now reports clearly when reticulate or anndata is missing, instead of failing with a bare there is no package called 'anndata'. Both are declared under Suggests.

Testing

  • Added a consolidated testthat suite — unit, module and browser tests — and a Tests GitHub Actions workflow that gates merges on it.
